prompt: The line $y = 4x - 8$ crosses the $x$-axis where $y = 0$. What is $x$ there?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Simpler: $y = 2x - 4$ hits zero when $2x = 4$, so $x = 2$. Set your $y$ to $0$ and solve the same way.
Add $8$ to both sides: $8 = 4x$. Then divide.

explanation: Divide by $4$: $x = 2$. The line crosses at $(2, 0)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Climb from the start
steps: The line starts at $(0, -8)$, which is $8$ below the $x$-axis, and climbs $4$ per step.
It needs $8 \div 4 = 2$ steps to reach height $0$ — so it crosses at $x = 2$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: −8 is the y-intercept — where the line crosses the OTHER axis — and it is the classic mix-up here.
Crossing the x-axis means y = 0: solve 4x − 8 = 0 to get x = 2. Which axis you cross decides which letter is zero.
